description: Run about 260 customer VMs on the hypervisor cluster and storage array at DC-1, including Bank A's loan document imaging and file server VMs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An outage of about 7.3 hours in a month drops availability below 99.0% and triggers the 25% credit tier for affected customers. Bank A's covered services sit on this platform, so an outage likely to last 4 hours or more requires a bank notice determination (12 CFR 53.4(a)). RPO is the nightly backup, and only for the 145 VMs on the backup add-on; other customers back up their own VMs under the MSA
manual_workaround: Move VMs from a failed host to the remaining 5 hosts (cluster capacity allows one host down). No site-level workaround: if DC-1 is lost, add-on VMs can only be restored into the cloud tenant (SYS-04), which has never been tried
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-02; SYS-07 (VPN sign-in for engineers)
dependent_third_parties: Colocation provider (power, cooling, bandwidth, remote hands); hardware vendor (next-business-day parts); MDR provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Lead Systems Engineer; 2 Systems Engineers; DC-1 cage access (badge and biometric)

description: Customers order, start, stop, reboot, and console into VMs, open tickets, and pay invoices through SYS-01, which drives the hypervisor manager API
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Running VMs keep running without the portal. After a business day, customers cannot reboot or reach the console of their own VMs, and support volume exceeds what 2 Support Engineers can handle. The nightly database dump sets a 24-hour RPO for orders and tickets
manual_workaround: Engineers perform urgent VM actions directly in the hypervisor manager on a customer's phone or email request (verified by call-back); invoices wait
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider; portal software vendor (license and updates)

description: Host and change about 190 customer DNS zones through the SaaS DNS provider account
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers' websites and email stop resolving when DNS fails. Resolution is the DNS provider's job; the company's risk is losing control of the account (takeover or deletion). There is no copy of the zones outside the provider, so today the real RPO is unknown
manual_workaround: Rebuild urgent zones by hand from customer records and tickets; ask customers to point to their registrar's DNS temporarily
dependent_third_parties: SaaS DNS provider; domain registrars (customers' own accounts)

business_process: Managed server services through the RMM tool
description: Monthly patching, monitoring alerts, and backup checks on about 310 servers of 22 customers, including 8 Bank A branch servers and 9 Bank B servers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patching can slip a few days without harm. After any compromise the tool must be validated before it is trusted again (P08), so a fast restore is not the goal. Bank servers are covered services: a 4-hour disruption caused by a security incident in the tool triggers the bank notice determination even though this process tolerates 72 hours
manual_workaround: Customers' own staff or the company's engineers use each customer's remote access with the customer's approval; patching resumes after validation

business_process: Customer support, after-hours on-call, and incident communication
description: Answer tickets and calls, run the after-hours on-call rotation, and send maintenance and incident notices to customers and banks
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers must reach the company during any outage. Bank notices are due as soon as possible after the 4-hour determination, and the MSA notice within 72 hours of confirmation, so communication must work even when other systems are down
manual_workaround: Calls to the support line forward to the on-call engineer's mobile phone; notices sent from a personal-device mail client using the printed contact list in the incident kit
dependent_third_parties: PSA vendor; productivity suite vendor; phone carrier
dependent_people_or_facilities: Support Engineers; Operations Manager; on-call engineer

description: Nightly backups of the 145 add-on VMs to the backup appliance with a copy to cloud object storage; restores on customer request
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers who lose data expect a restore the same business day. The nightly schedule sets a 24-hour RPO. The local appliance is at DC-1, so a site loss leaves only the cloud copy
manual_workaround: Restore from the cloud copy if the appliance fails; the order of customers is set by the Owner
dependent_third_parties: Public cloud provider; backup software vendor

description: 24x7 monitoring of laptops, identity provider, and firewall logs by the MDR provider, with escalations to the on-call engineer
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A day without monitoring is tolerable only if no incident is under way. The MDR keeps the collected logs; the company keeps nothing locally
manual_workaround: EDR agents keep blocking known malware on their own; the on-call engineer checks identity provider sign-in alerts by email

description: Invoicing and collections (portal billing module and the processor's hosted page), payroll through a payroll service, contracts and HR files in the productivity suite
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Invoices can go out a week late; payroll runs biweekly and the cash reserve covers about 45 days of expenses
manual_workaround: Invoice from the prior month's usage; repeat the prior payroll through the payroll service
dependent_third_parties: Payment processor; payroll service; productivity suite vendor
